title: Coconut Rice
author: Fran Osseo-Asare
desc: Published at three scales with three appliances — one cup in a microwave, three in a rice cooker, sixteen in an oven for sixty people.
longDesc: The same cook gives coconut rice three ways, and the scaling is the real information. One cup of rice in the microwave at fifty per cent power for fifteen to twenty minutes with the vent holes open, then five minutes' rest. Three cups in a rice cooker with a cup and a half of coconut milk and three and a half to four cups of water. Or sixteen cups of washed rice with two tins of coconut milk and about thirty cups of water, baked at 375 degrees for forty-five minutes to an hour across two covered pans — enough for about sixty people at a quarter cup of rice each.
ingredients: 1 tbsp coconut cream mixed with enough coconut milk to replace 1/2 cup of the water
1 1/2 tbsp salt — 1/4 tsp for each cup of rice
equipment: Microwave with a vented lid, rice cooker, or oven with two covered pans
Large pot, for boiling the oven batch's water
steps: Mix 1 tablespoon of the coconut cream with enough coconut milk to replace 1/2 cup of the water, and combine with the rice and the remaining water.
Cook covered at 50 per cent (medium) for about 15 to 20 minutes, with the vent holes in the lid open.
Combine 3 cups rice, 1 1/2 cups coconut milk, 3 1/2 to 4 cups water, the optional cream and the optional turmeric.
Allow 1/4 teaspoon of salt for each cup of rice, about 1 1/2 tablespoons in all.
Combine the washed rice, the 2 tins of coconut milk and about 30 cups of boiling water across two covered pans.
Bake at 375 degrees for 45 minutes to an hour.
After about 30 minutes open the oven and carefully tilt and lift the lids.
chefTips: The three scales are the real lesson: a microwave for one cup, a rice cooker for three, an oven for sixteen. Coconut milk scorches on a hob, which is why the big batch goes in the oven.
Fifty per cent power in the microwave, not full. Coconut milk boils over at full power and the vent holes stay open for the same reason.
The oven batch is quarter-cup-per-person party catering — sixteen cups of rice feeds about sixty. That is a genuinely useful figure and almost nobody publishes it.
Lift the lids at the thirty-minute mark on the oven batch. Tilt them carefully; the trapped steam is the dangerous part.
A quarter teaspoon of salt per cup of rice is the scaling rule, and it works at every size.
Turmeric is optional and is for colour. One printing gives half a teaspoon and another half to one teaspoon, so start low.
Coconut cream plus coconut milk, not just milk — the cream is what makes it rich. Her companion recipe covers extracting both from a fresh coconut.
commonMistakes: Full power in the microwave, which boils it over.
Cooking sixteen cups on a hob, where the milk catches.
Dropping the lids flat and getting a steam burn at the thirty-minute check.
Salting by taste at party scale rather than by the per-cup rule.
sources: Adapted from 'Recipe #56 (Coconut rice, 3 ways) and #57 (Coconut smoothie)', betumiblog.blogspot.com. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Posted by Fran at 12:23 PM', timestamped 2011-06-21T12:23:00-05:00.

MICROWAVE VERSION, TWO-PASS: '1 cup of white rice' with '1 tablespoon of the coconut cream mixed with enough coconut milk to replace 1/2 cup of the water'; cook 'at 50% (medium) for about 15-20 minutes, covered, with the vent holes in the lid open', then rest 'another 5 minutes or so'. The '1-1.5 cups water' figure and the 4-serving yield are SINGLE-PASS.

RICE COOKER VERSION, TWO-PASS: '3 cups' rice, '1 1/2 cups of coconut milk', optional few tablespoons of cream, '3.5 to 4 cups of water'. Turmeric '1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml)' TWO-PASS; a turmeric-or-saffron range of '1/2-1 teaspoon' is SINGLE-PASS and the two figures differ, so both are recorded and neither is corrected.

OVEN VERSION, TWO-PASS on these items: '16 cups of rice (already washed)', '2 cans of coconut milk with cream', '~30 cups of water'; salt '1/4 teaspoon for each cup of rice, or ~1 1/2 Tablespoons'; '375 degrees F' for '45 minutes to an hour'; and 'After about 30 minutes open the oven, carefully tilt and lift the lids'.

A MISPRINT FLAGGED AND NOT FIXED: one pass reads 'boil 32 cups water' while the recipe lists about 30 cups, and 14-15 cups of liquid per pan across two pans comes to 28-30. The yield of about 60 people at a quarter cup of rice each is SINGLE-PASS.

COMPANION RECIPES from the same author and same week: '#54 Chilled coconut water' and '#55 Coconut cream and milk' — the latter published here at GHA113, and the source of the fresh coconut milk and cream this recipe assumes. Also '#57 Coconut smoothie', TWO-PASS: 1 cup frozen pineapple chunks, 1 frozen banana in chunks, 4 or 5 ice cubes, an inch of vanilla bean or 1/2 to 1 tsp extract, and 1 cup of rich coconut milk, credited on the page to her daughter Masi. The smoothie is not published separately.
NO DONENESS CUE beyond the times and the lid-lifting check is printed for any of the three versions. That absence is recorded.

THIS IS THE ONLY DOCUMENTED GHANAIAN COCONUT RICE in the material consulted. This collection separately documents a NIGERIAN fried coconut rice by a different author, which is a declared British-Nigerian hybrid and a different dish.
The four servings above corresponds to the microwave scale, which is the only one of the three with a printed yield.
storage: 3 days refrigerated. Coconut rice firms up considerably.
reheating: Steam, or microwave with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Coconut provides medium-chain fats that are metabolised differently from long-chain.
Lower in sodium than most savoury rice dishes.
Coconut milk adds manganese and copper.
culturalNote: Coconut palms line the Ghanaian coast and coconut rice is the natural result — sweet, rich, and served beside something hot. The jump from a microwave cup to sixteen cups in an oven is also a quiet record of how Ghanaian cooking scales for a party, which is most of the time.
